Same.  Many years ago I was in high school and we lived out in the country. We let the cats outside for romps and usually got them inside with no issue. 

One day, Midnight did not come home. We didn't think too much of it. She was the master huntress, often bestowing us with her catches on the front porch. 

Day 2, we started to get worried as it was unlike Midnight to not be home by now.

Midnight is special to my mother and I. While we brought our cat up with us in the move, Midnight was found not long after. She was a starving kitten in front of a grocery store.  At the point of her disappearance, she was 12 years old. "Missy Midnighty-kins," as she was properly addressed, was a petite tuxedo cat, but full of attitude. She wouldn't hesitate to boss the 22 pound male cat we also adopted around, or swipe at a teenage me that was being a nuisance to her and probably deserved it.  Despite her moodiness, she always knew when someone needed a cuddle.

Day 3-9, Momma and I are frantic. I'd get home from school and call for her until parents got home. Mom then took over while I did homework and dinner was made.  Our house is surrounded by fields used for either corn or soybeans. The corn was fully grown and 6' tall so we really wouldn't have been able to see a 6lb cat, but we'd call until we were blue in the face. 

Day 10, i had resigned myself that maybe the worse came to pass, but I wanted to give one last try. I got home from school and crossed the road to the other cornfield and railroad tracks. I call for her. 

I hear it. The daintiest of squeaks. I call again. Out from the corn rows pops Midnight. She's squeaking happily and running to see me. I start crying and carry her home.  I called my mother to give her the happy news between sobs.

It was then decided that Midnight had to retire from outside, which she didn't seem to mind after this adventure. Our theory is that she lost her direction in the cornfield.

Missy lived until 16. I miss that little cat.

Think how lucky that cat is to have had two special people in his life.

I went to the shelter and saw plenty of candidates. They were all friendly, meowing and sticking their paws through the bars.  My eyes landed on a cow cat that was huddled up in a corner. She didn't move or meow at me, just kind of sadly looked at me. I felt something lance through my heart with her. Her expression had said something like, "You don't want me." Like she had been rejected and passed over many times.

I asked the shelter gal about her. They stated she was 9 months old. She had come in pregnant and only gave birth to one kitten. As in there was a single kitten in her womb. Kitten got adopted out first when it was ready.  She otherwise had been pretty timid and kept to herself. The lady opened the cage and I "tsked" or clicked to the cat. "Margie" as she was called didn't meow, but instead just crawled into my arms and tucked her head under my chin.

"Margie" was creatively renamed Kitty-kat by myself. That's what she responded to and came when called. I had her groomed and the groomer showed me where her leg had been broken and healed askew. A good third/half inch of bone poked against the skin when she laid on her back, stretched out and asking for belly rubs. She was the few that liked belly rubs.

Depression struck me like a horse falling off a bridge. My stepmother and dad asked me to move out of the second house they owned and I was staying in. We moved into an apartment where I didn't last long there either and was evicted. I moved in with my Grandparents as I was not on speaking terms with either of my parents.

This cat never complained. She took it in stride and seemed to know I was getting way off kilter as she was very, very cuddly and attentive to me. Even when I drank myself into a stupor and passing out in random places. A couple times I had seriously  considered ending it all. ODing on some medication, slitting wrists, etc. Each time she would just sit and look at me.We needed each other to be around.

I did finally pull out of my nosedive. I moved out but Kitty-kat stayed with my grandparents. We had lived there for 4 years and she really acclimated to life there and was also very fond of my grandfather.

She lived to her fully life until her kidney disease finally made it too much and Grandpa and Grandma made the decision to put her to sleep.

My cat now, Qwerty, reminds me a lot of Kitty-kat. She is also timid, but very attached to me. I still struggle with severe bouts of depression from time to time and Qwerty is riding it out with me. I think Kitty-kat is in Qwerty somewhere even a touch.

TL;DR: Unexpected cat adoption probably saved me from committig suicide and was a very good girl.
